single_artifact_test.decision_rule: Classify exact stream recoverability as evidenced only if path A is complete or path B is complete in the single inspected primary artifact together with already frozen role-local facts. Otherwise keep status unresolved_not_exactly_recoverable_from_currently_inspected_evidence; never infer global unrecoverability from absence in one artifact.
single_artifact_test.duplicate_effect_rule: Do not rewrite predecessor or preflight artifacts; each inspected artifact gets one uniquely named terminal checkpoint bound to its exact source identity.
single_artifact_test.forgetting_and_rollback_relevance: A durable continual-learning checkpoint that preserves aggregate metrics but omits the ordered stream or deterministic reconstruction ingredients cannot guarantee exact replay after rollback or cross-run reconstruction.

tested_scope: Only the acceptance logic for one future primary artifact inspection was materialized from existing role-local evidence. No new public source, released repository file, dataset listing, second table, O state, other worker output, downstream state, or external compute was consumed.
continuation: Next invocation, after exact authority/bootstrap and role-local reconstruction, first preserve this acceptance test. If persistence-recovery lifecycle still forbids public/external calls, inspect exactly one own role-local predecessor/source-locator artifact to recover the identity of a primary NC-TFAD released code/config or stream-construction source without consuming its external contents; persist that single locator result and stop. If the active lifecycle instead permits one public-source leaf, inspect exactly one identified primary artifact against path A/path B and persist the exact source identity, matched/missing fields, tested scope and unresolved/pass classification. Do not inspect a second artifact or table in the same slice; preserve CLEAN isolation, zero residual richer-mode/protected/user execution dependency, zero finite quota and zero incremental cost.
